record.original_question: Does there exist a group G that contains a family(Gn)n∈N of finite-index subgroups such that for every n there is a homomorphism fn: Gn → Z whose kernel is of type Fn, but not of type Fn+1?

evidence.quote: Does there exist a group G that contains a family(Gn)n∈N of finite-index subgroups such that for every n there is a homomorphism fn: Gn → Z whose kernel is of type Fn, but not of type Fn+1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a group H is said to be of type F_n if it admits an Eilenberg–MacLane space K(H,1) with finitely many cells in dimensions ≤ n; equivalently, H acts freely and cocompactly on the n-skeleton of some contractible CW complex. Type F_1 coincides with finite generation, type F_2 with finite presentability, and being of type F_n for all n is denoted F_∞.

Question: Does there exist a group G together with a family (G_n)_{n ∈ ℕ} of finite-index subgroups of G and, for each n ∈ ℕ, a homomorphism f_n : G_n → ℤ such that the kernel ker(f_n) is of type F_n but not of type F_{n+1}?
